title: Chapter 5
content:
Outside the high-rise window, Bangkok’s night skyline glittered in a brilliant wave of neon and concrete. A landscape that had felt alien when he first arrived now offered the quiet comfort of home. Then again, when you didn't have a place of your own, anywhere you stayed long enough became home. Savoring the quiet nostalgia, Jakyeong pulled a cigarette from his pack and lit it up.

Right on cue, Wang Han ambled over holding two chilled bottles of beer he’d snatched from the fridge, handing one over.

"What’s got you looking so lost in thought?"

"Just wondering if I'll ever see this place again."

Wang Han’s forehead creased into a deep scowl. "Don't jinx it, man."

Jakyeong offered a faint smile, taking a smooth pull of his beer. Tomorrow afternoon, he’d need to step out and handle some business. Get a clean haircut, pick up a second pair of glasses, buy a few tame, harmless-looking outfits. Maybe hit up his favorite local spot for one last solid meal, too.

"How long has it been since you were back in Korea? Five years?"

"Yeah."

"How are you feeling about it?"

"Hard to say..."

Wang Han didn't press further. He’d heard enough to know the nightmare Jakyeong had endured growing up in Korea. Both of his parents had been low-level criminals mixed up in the drug trade. While kids his age were sitting in classrooms, Jakyeong was being used as a runner for drug deliveries. Starvation and beatings were a daily routine; the luxury of having a dream wasn't something he was ever allowed to entertain.

Then his parents died, leaving ten-year-old Jakyeong utterly alone until Wang Han’s father took him in. Twelve years his senior, Wang Han raised the boy like his own flesh and blood, but with criminality as their only inheritance, both ended up in the underworld anyway.

"What are you gonna do once we get paid?" Jakyeong asked.

"I’m thinking about getting a hair transplant this time," Wang Han said thoughtfully. "What do you think?"

Jakyeong burst into a sudden, incredulous laugh. A while back, Wang Han had bought some dodgy hair growth tonic online. He’d applied it incorrectly, causing hair to sprout on his palms—forcing him to shave the insides of his hands with a razor for weeks. Only later did he read the tiny warning label instructing him to wash his hands thoroughly after application.

"Give it up," Jakyeong chuckled. "If there were a magic cure for baldness, there wouldn't be a single bald billionaire on the planet."

Unable to argue with facts, Wang Han grunted softly. "Fine. What about you then? You still set on buying that island?"

"Who knows." Jakyeong pressed the cool rim of the beer bottle against his lower lip, musing for a moment. "Maybe I'll donate it."

"Donate it?"

"Yeah. Like Warren Buffett."

"Classy," Wang Han nodded with deadpan sincerity. "He’s the undisputed king of investing, and you’re the undisputed king of contract killing. In a way, you two are practically peers."

Wang Han was completely serious, but Jakyeong just offered a dry, self-deprecating smile. If Warren Buffett found out he was being compared to a human butcher, the old man would probably die of rage. Buffett was revered world-wide; Jakyeong only ever received gratitude when someone wanted a corpse.

Wang Han raised his bottle high. "To you—a man destined to be greater than Warren Buffett."

Jakyeong laughed, clinking his bottle against Wang Han’s. "To five million dollars—and your new head of hair."

The sharp, relentless blare of an alarm pierced the silence. With his eyes still closed, Il-hyun stretched an arm out and slapped the stop button.

7:00 AM.

He sat up on the edge of the bed, rubbing his face vigorously to chase away the fog. He’d been out late into the night drinking with politicians, leaving him with a heavy, persistent hangover that sleep hadn't managed to cure.

Every instinct urged him to fall back onto the pillows, but his morning schedule left no room for slacking. Throwing a silk robe over his bare skin, he stepped out into the living room.

Tae-soo immediately stood up from the sofa. "Good morning, Executive Director."

"You're early," Il-hyun rasped, his voice rough with fatigue.

He walked over to the dry bar in the corner and opened the mini-fridge, which was fully stocked with single-serve water bottles and beer. Grabbing a water, he twisted the cap off and chugged it down, quenching the burning thirst in his throat.

"What time does his flight land?"

"10:30 AM, sir."

Perfect timing if he showered and left now. Tossing the empty plastic bottle into the trash, Il-hyun shed his robe, stepped into the bathroom, and let a cold shower blast over him. He stood motionless beneath the freezing cascade for a long time with his eyes closed, letting his head clear.

Stepping out, he dried off, blow-dried his hair, slapped on some toner, and perused his closet. Selecting a crisp, ice-blue dress shirt, he paired it with a matching luxury watch and tie before stepping in front of the full-length mirror.

As he fastened his cufflinks, he flashed a smooth, devastatingly handsome smile at his reflection, rehearsing his greeting as if the mark were standing right before him:

"Welcome to Korea."

He tilted his head from side to side, inspecting his reflection. Hmm. Looking good.

Satisfied, he grabbed his suit jacket and walked out into the hall, where Tae-soo was waiting.

"Let's move."

The two men traversed the long second-floor corridor toward the grand central staircase. Every step they took was captured in real-time by the estate’s security network. Ever since the hit squad ambushed his residence four years ago, Il-hyun had the entire villa outfitted with high-grade security cameras featuring night-vision motion sensors.

Five men had died in his home that night—two of his own guards and three assassins. Il-hyun had left one assassin alive long enough to inflict unimaginable torture, forcing him to surrender his employer's name. The following year, a prominent congressman was found dead in his sedan, ruled a suicide.

"Good morning, Executive Director," the resident staff chanted in unison, bowing deeply as Il-hyun descended the stairs.

"Morning," he acknowledged smoothly.

From the kitchen, an elderly woman wearing an apron hurried out to greet him. She was the housekeeper—a woman who had watched Il-hyun grow up since he was a toddler taking his very first steps.

"Ah, Young Master. You're up."

"Don't worry about breakfast today, Auntie. I'm heading straight to the airport."

"At least let me whip up something quick for the road—"

"No need. Don't trouble yourself."

"I heard we have a guest arriving today...?"

"Yes. He'll be staying with us for a while. Please take good care of him."

"Of course, sir."

Flashing her a gentle smile, Il-hyun stepped outside with Tae-soo. Crossing the expansive lawn, they approached the sedan waiting by the front gates.

Il-hyun slid into the back seat, sinking into the leather as his hangover flared back up, twisting his stomach in knots. He pinched the bridge of his nose—a subtle gesture Tae-soo caught instantly in the rearview mirror.

"Are you alright, sir?"

Il-hyun gave a single nod.

The car glided forward, leaving the private neighborhood behind. As they passed a city park, the morning sun lit up the green space. Despite the early hour, a fair crowd was out enjoying the spring weather—couples in light spring jackets strolling hand-in-hand, families soaking up the morning warmth.

Just past the park, Il-hyun caught sight of a florist shop and raised a hand. "Stop the car."

Tae-soo glanced back, surprised. "Sir?"

"Go grab some flowers."

"Flowers, sir?"

"A guest coming from so far away deserves a proper welcome, don't you think?"

Without another word, Tae-soo stepped out and crossed into the flower shop. After a brief exchange with the florist, he returned carrying a lush bouquet of red roses, looking for all the world like a regular guy on his way to a romantic date.

As the car resumed its journey, Il-hyun closed his eyes and leaned back against the headrest. The heavy fatigue and lingering alcohol finally pulled him into a light sleep.

What felt like a split-second nap ended as the car pulled onto the airport expressway. Il-hyun opened his eyes, cracked his neck from side to side, and checked his watch. Right on time.

Ten minutes later, the sedan pulled up to the arrivals terminal. Stepping out into the morning breeze, Il-hyun took the roses from Tae-soo. The heady, sweet scent of red roses wafted up. In Il-hyun's world, he only ever touched flowers on two occasions: when someone died, or when there was something to celebrate.

Inside, the terminal was surprisingly quiet. Standing near the gate, Il-hyun held the bouquet in one hand and a welcome sign written in Cantonese in the other: Jang Yi-an.

The flight monitor flashed green, indicating the Hong Kong flight had landed. Moments later, passengers began trickling through the sliding doors.

Scanning the emerging crowd, Il-hyun’s eyes settled on a tall figure walking out. The young man wore a green plaid shirt and round, silver-rimmed glasses. His shoulders were slightly stooped, and his wide, naive eyes darted nervously around the terminal like a lost puppy. A heavily built bodyguard trailed right beside him, lugging his designer luggage.

"That him?" Il-hyun asked softly.

Tae-soo pulled a photograph from his inner jacket pocket, verifying the face. "Yes, sir. That's him."

Without hesitation, Il-hyun stepped forward, bouquet in hand, closing the distance until he stood directly in front of the youth.

Up close, the kid wasn't particularly towering—a little over six feet, at most. Looking down at the slightly shorter man, Il-hyun watched as the youth raised his head, their eyes locking. Behind the round spectacles, the boy's eyes widened in clear surprise. Curiously, the skin around his lower eyelids was naturally flushed red, giving them a perpetually moist, vulnerable look.

"I am Kang Il-hyun," he introduced smoothly. "Welcome to Korea."

Offering the bouquet, Il-hyun watched as the boy glanced nervously at his bodyguard. The guard gave a firm nod.

Jang Yi-an—or rather, Lee Ja-kyeong disguised as Jang Yi-an—accepted the flowers.

Il-hyun immediately extended his right hand. "Pleasure to meet you."

Hesitating for a heartbeat, Jakyeong carefully reached out and took his hand. "Pleasure to meet you too," he murmured in Cantonese, offering an awkward, timid smile.

Kang Il-hyun’s hand was bone-chillingly cold—like touching the belly of a live snake.

Feeling the grip linger a second too long, Jakyeong tried to pull his hand back, but Il-hyun didn't let go. Jakyeong’s expression stiffened. Sensing the shift in mood, the bodyguard brought over from Hong Kong stepped forward aggressively.

[Watch your manners,] the guard barked in Cantonese.
